Postgraduate Earth Science
Study the Earth—its structure, history, and the forces that continue to shape it.
Overview
Qualifications
People
The Earth Sciences are a window into the way planet Earth operates, both past and present.
Work with Aotearoa New Zealand’s top-ranked Earth Science group, alongside world-class researchers. You'll build expertise through field and laboratory research while developing strong communication skills.
Our strong links with Earth Sciences New Zealand connect you to the wider Wellington geoscience community. This opens up a diverse range of research opportunities.
Available qualifications
Bachelor of Science with Honours
Postgraduate Certificate in Science
Postgraduate Diploma in Science
Master of Science by coursework and thesis
Master of Science by thesis
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)
Earth history
The best place to study
Aotearoa lies across the boundary between two of the great shifting tectonic plates. It’s an outstanding natural laboratory to study the dynamic processes that shape our country and planet.
The rocks beneath our feet tell us about Earth’s history. Present-day geological observations measure the forces shaping our planet. Geophysical techniques image beneath the surface, even down to the Earth’s core.
We apply our knowledge of the past alongside our observations of the present to understand natural hazards, resources, and climate.
Globally ranked
This programme is ranked in the top 150 worldwide in the QS World University Rankings 2026.
The QS World University Rankings is an annual global publication that gives overall rankings and subject rankings for more than 1,500 universities worldwide.
Learn from experts
Your lecturers and tutors are leaders in the field of Earth Sciences. They’ve received global recognition in their disciplines through Fellowships, awards, and society leaderships.
Our staff regularly secure competitive funding for nationally and internationally significant research, including through the Ngā Ngaru Wakapuke and ECLIPSE programmes. We publish in leading journals, and our strong connections across Aotearoa's research and policy sectors help ensure our work has real-world impact.
Careers
A qualification in the Earth Sciences can take you into interesting and important roles—both in Aotearoa New Zealand and overseas. You might find work:
at a private consultancy
in the government sector as a scientific adviser
in the mining or mineral exploration sector
in a role identifying and mitigating natural hazards at a Public Research Organisation.
Regardless of your position, the quantitative and thinking skills that you will learn in the Earth Sciences will serve you well in a huge variety of other occupations.
See what you can do with a degree in Earth Sciences
Join our postgraduate community
Postgraduate study at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington will help you build valuable relationships with peers, academics, clinical experts, and professional colleagues. You’ll have opportunities to attend events, seminars, workshops, and social functions.
The Postgraduate Students' Association offers information on study at the University and provides a voice for you on campus.

Financial support
You can get support to stay on top of your finances by downloading our money management resources or by meeting with one of our student finance advisers.
We can show you how to manage your student loan or allowance, and help you sort out your budget. For students facing financial difficulties, we can help you apply for support from the Hardship Fund. Depending on your situation, you might also be able to get government or community support.
